questions.q: Why might you connect directly to a database instead of exporting to a file first?
options: Databases cannot be queried directly under any circumstances
Exporting to a file is always faster and should always be preferred
There is no real difference between the two approaches
Direct connection always sees current data and lets the database engine handle filtering and sorting efficiently, rather than pulling everything into Python first
questions.explain: An exported file can go stale the moment the source table is updated.

questions.q: Why does closing a database connection belong in a finally block?
options: finally blocks are required by pyodbc and have no other purpose
The connection closes whether the query succeeded or failed, avoiding a leaked open connection if something goes wrong mid-query
Connections close themselves automatically with no code needed
finally only matters for file operations, never database connections
questions.explain: This is Lesson 19's exception-handling pattern applied directly to a real database connection.
